title.narrative: Tejedoras de Derechos, Buen Vivir y Democracia en Guatemala

description.narrative: The project generates a transformative impact by promoting the individual and collective rights of plural women, young people and indigenous peoples towards Good Living and full democracy in Guatemala, strengthening their economic, political and personal autonomy for the effective exercise of ESCERs. Women's, indigenous and feminist organizations are consolidated as territorial political references, providing them with greater capacities for leadership, management, accountability and institutional sustainability, which allows them to strategically influence the defense of their rights and territories. Through emancipatory economic alternatives, access to sustainable livelihoods is expanded, recognizing care work as a fundamental contribution to the economy and community well-being, improving health, safety and healing conditions. With a transformative gender approach, female and youth leadership, equitable political participation and the breaking of patriarchal power relations are promoted, guaranteeing a life free of violence. In contexts of high climate vulnerability, the project reinforces climate justice by actively defending territories against extractivism and dispossession, increasing community resilience and balance with nature. Thus, more just, resilient and sovereign environments are built where women and young people, especially indigenous people, carry out full and dignified life projects.
